_note: Concept cars, shown in the Database 'Cars' tab next to cars.json. 'wiki' is the English Wikipedia article whose lead image and summary are shown.

concepts.name: Dymaxion car
concepts.fact: A three-wheeled teardrop that steered with its single rear wheel; only three were built.

concepts.name: Volvo Venus Bilo
concepts.fact: A streamlined 1930s Volvo study that pointed the way to the PV36 Carioca.

concepts.name: Buick Y-Job
concepts.fact: Widely considered the car industry's first concept car. Harley Earl used it as his personal daily driver.

concepts.name: Phantom Corsair
concepts.fact: A one-off six-seater built by a Heinz ketchup heir, with push-button doors and no door handles.

concepts.name: General Motors Le Sabre
concepts.fact: A rain sensor raised its soft top automatically, and Harley Earl drove it as his own car.

concepts.name: Alfa Romeo BAT
concepts.fact: BAT stands for Berlinetta Aerodinamica Tecnica: three aerodynamic studies (BAT 5, 7 and 9) with dramatic curved tail fins.

concepts.name: Fiat Turbina
concepts.fact: Italy's first gas-turbine car; its drag coefficient of 0.14 stood as a record for decades.

concepts.name: Ford FX-Atmos
concepts.fact: A jet-age show car with a clear bubble canopy, shown at the 1954 Chicago Auto Show.

concepts.name: Pontiac Bonneville Special
concepts.fact: A fibreglass two-seater with a bubble canopy, built for GM's 1954 Motorama show.

concepts.name: Lincoln Futura
concepts.fact: George Barris turned it into the Batmobile for the 1966 Batman TV series.

concepts.name: Pontiac Club de Mer
concepts.fact: A low two-seater with twin bubble windscreens, built for GM's 1956 Motorama show.

concepts.name: Ford Nucleon
concepts.fact: Meant to be powered by a small nuclear reactor in the back. Only a scale model was ever built.

concepts.name: Cadillac Cyclone
concepts.fact: Radar units in its nose cones were meant to warn the driver of obstacles ahead.

concepts.name: Plymouth XNR
concepts.fact: Deliberately asymmetric: a long hump runs over the driver's side only.

concepts.name: Chevrolet Mako Shark
concepts.fact: Painted to fade from blue to white like a shark, it previewed the 1963 Corvette Sting Ray.

concepts.name: Chevrolet Corvair Monza GT
concepts.fact: A mid-engined coupé built on Corvair parts, with a canopy instead of conventional doors.

concepts.name: Ford Mustang I
concepts.fact: A mid-engined two-seater that first carried the Mustang name, yet looks nothing like the production car.

concepts.name: Chevrolet Testudo
concepts.fact: Designed by a young Giorgetto Giugiaro at Bertone on a Chevrolet Corvair chassis.

concepts.name: Chrysler Turbine Car
concepts.fact: Gas-turbine powered; Chrysler lent them to ordinary families for road testing, then destroyed most of them.

concepts.name: GM-X Stiletto
concepts.fact: A fighter-jet-inspired two-seater from GM's Futurama show at the 1964 New York World's Fair.

concepts.name: Vauxhall XVR
concepts.fact: A low, wedge-shaped two-seater: Vauxhall's first true dream car.

concepts.name: Bertone Pirana
concepts.fact: Built on Jaguar E-Type mechanicals for a British newspaper's motor show stand.

concepts.name: Dodge Deora
concepts.fact: A custom Dodge A100 pickup you enter through the front. It became one of the first Hot Wheels cars in 1968.

concepts.name: Lamborghini Marzal
concepts.fact: Almost fully glazed gullwing doors and a straight-six made from half of Lamborghini's V12.

concepts.name: Alfa Romeo Carabo
concepts.fact: Named after the Carabus beetle. Its wedge shape and scissor doors pointed straight at the Lamborghini Countach.

concepts.name: Bizzarrini Manta
concepts.fact: Giugiaro's first car at Italdesign, with three seats side by side and the driver in the middle.

concepts.name: Alfa Romeo Iguana
concepts.fact: Built on the Alfa Romeo 33 Stradale chassis, with a brushed stainless-steel body.

concepts.name: Holden Hurricane
concepts.fact: Australia's mid-engined dream car, with a canopy roof and an early route-finding system.

concepts.name: Mercedes-Benz C111
concepts.fact: An experimental test bed that ran Wankel rotary engines, then diesel engines that set speed records in the late 1970s.

concepts.name: AMC AMX/3
concepts.fact: A mid-engined American supercar developed with Giotto Bizzarrini; only a handful were built.

concepts.name: Ferrari Modulo
concepts.fact: There are no doors: the whole canopy slides forward to let you in.

concepts.name: Lancia Stratos Zero
concepts.fact: It is only about 84 cm (33 in) tall, and you get in through the hinged windscreen.

concepts.name: Mazda RX-500
concepts.fact: A mid-engined rotary study whose tail lights changed colour to show if it was speeding up or braking.

concepts.name: Vauxhall SRV
concepts.fact: A mid-engined 'Styling Research Vehicle' that hid four doors inside its low wedge.

concepts.name: BMW Turbo
concepts.fact: A gullwing safety-research concept shown for the 1972 Munich Olympics. Its ideas returned in the BMW M1.

concepts.name: Maserati Boomerang
concepts.fact: The steering wheel rim turned around a fixed hub that held all the gauges.

concepts.name: Chevrolet Aerovette
concepts.fact: A mid-engined Corvette that nearly reached production in the 1970s. The mid-engined Corvette finally arrived with the C8.

concepts.name: Lamborghini Bravo
concepts.fact: A compact Bertone wedge on Urraco mechanicals, intended as an Urraco replacement.

concepts.name: Maserati Medici
concepts.fact: A large four-door Maserati saloon study by Italdesign.

concepts.name: Lancia Sibilo
concepts.fact: Built on Stratos mechanicals, with windows that flow into the bodywork without a visible frame.

concepts.name: Aston Martin Bulldog
concepts.fact: Built to reach 200 mph. It only managed that decades later, after a full restoration.

concepts.name: Citroën Karin
concepts.fact: A pyramid-shaped car with three seats in a row and the driver in the middle.

concepts.name: Ferrari Pinin
concepts.fact: A four-door Ferrari saloon with a flat-12, made for Pininfarina's 50th anniversary.

concepts.name: Lamborghini Athon
concepts.fact: An open two-seater shown at Turin in 1980, while Lamborghini itself was close to bankruptcy.

concepts.name: Lotus Etna
concepts.fact: A Giugiaro-designed supercar planned around a new Lotus V8. It never reached production.

concepts.name: Nissan MID4
concepts.fact: Mid-engined, four-wheel drive and four-wheel steering: a Japanese supercar Nissan never built.

concepts.name: Oldsmobile Aerotech
concepts.fact: A. J. Foyt drove it to a closed-course speed record of about 257 mph (414 km/h) in 1987.

concepts.name: Bertone Genesis
concepts.fact: A people carrier with a Lamborghini Countach V12 under the bonnet.

concepts.name: Italdesign Aztec
concepts.fact: Driver and passenger sit in two separate cockpits, each with its own windscreen.

concepts.name: Porsche 989
concepts.fact: A four-door Porsche saloon, cancelled in 1991, long before the Panamera.

concepts.name: Ferrari Mythos
concepts.fact: An open two-seater on Testarossa mechanicals, shown at the 1989 Tokyo Motor Show.

concepts.name: Audi Avus quattro
concepts.fact: Its mirror-polished aluminium body previewed Audi's aluminium cars; the W12 engine was a mock-up.

concepts.name: Mercedes-Benz C112
concepts.fact: A gullwing supercar with active aerodynamics; hundreds of buyers wanted one, but it was never built.

concepts.name: BMW Nazca C2
concepts.fact: Italdesign's carbon-bodied supercar study with a BMW V12.

concepts.name: Renault Zoom
concepts.fact: An electric two-seat city car whose rear wheels could fold in to make it shorter for parking.

concepts.name: Bugatti EB 112
concepts.fact: A four-door Bugatti with a V12, shown at Geneva in 1993.

concepts.name: Renault Racoon
concepts.fact: An amphibious off-roader that could drive straight into water.

concepts.name: Chrysler Atlantic
concepts.fact: A modern take on the Bugatti Type 57 Atlantic, with a straight-eight engine.

concepts.name: Ford GT90
concepts.fact: A quad-turbo V12 with a claimed 720 hp. Its 'New Edge' styling shaped Ford design in the late '90s.

concepts.name: Lamborghini Calà
concepts.fact: A V10 four-seater study, years before Lamborghini's V10 Gallardo.

concepts.name: Alfa Romeo Nuvola
concepts.fact: A retro-styled coupé whose chassis was designed to take different bodies.

concepts.name: Alfa Romeo Scighera
concepts.fact: A four-wheel-drive, twin-turbo V6 coupé built by Italdesign.

concepts.name: Dodge Copperhead
concepts.fact: A smaller, cheaper sports car meant to sit below the Viper.

concepts.name: Volkswagen W12
concepts.fact: The W12 Nardo version set a 24-hour world record in 2002, averaging more than 320 km/h.

concepts.name: Bugatti EB 118
concepts.fact: The first Bugatti under Volkswagen ownership, with a W18 engine.

concepts.name: Bentley Hunaudières
concepts.fact: A mid-engined W16 coupé; the engine idea later went into the Bugatti Veyron.

concepts.name: Bugatti 18/3 Chiron
concepts.fact: One of the W18 concepts that led to the Veyron.

concepts.name: Cadillac Evoq
concepts.fact: Previewed the Cadillac XLR roadster and the brand's sharp-edged new style.

concepts.name: Ford 021C
concepts.fact: A pastel city car by industrial designer Marc Newson rather than a car designer.

concepts.name: Audi Rosemeyer
concepts.fact: Named after the pre-war Auto Union racer Bernd Rosemeyer, with a W16 engine under the silver skin.

concepts.name: Volkswagen 1-litre car
concepts.fact: Built to use one litre of fuel per 100 km; the idea led to the VW XL1.

concepts.name: Audi Le Mans quattro
concepts.fact: Shown at Frankfurt in 2003; it became the Audi R8.

concepts.name: Cadillac Sixteen
concepts.fact: A 13.6-litre V16 rated at 1,000 hp, a nod to Cadillac's V-16 cars of the 1930s.

concepts.name: Chrysler ME Four-Twelve
concepts.fact: Four turbos and twelve cylinders: an AMG-sourced 6.0-litre V12 with a claimed 850 hp.

concepts.name: Peugeot Quark
concepts.fact: A fuel-cell quad bike with an electric motor in each wheel.

concepts.name: Rolls-Royce 100EX
concepts.fact: A V16 convertible for Rolls-Royce's centenary that led to the Phantom Drophead Coupé.

concepts.name: Volvo YCC
concepts.fact: 'Your Concept Car' was designed by a team of women at Volvo; even the oil check was left to the dealer.

concepts.name: Ford Shelby GR-1
concepts.fact: A polished-aluminium coupé built on Ford GT mechanicals.

concepts.name: Holden Efijy
concepts.fact: A modern custom car based on the 1953 Holden FJ.

concepts.name: Maserati Birdcage 75th
concepts.fact: Built for Pininfarina's 75th anniversary on Maserati MC12 mechanicals.

concepts.name: Mercedes-Benz Bionic
concepts.fact: Its shape was copied from the boxfish.

concepts.name: Peugeot Moovie
concepts.fact: A two-seat electric pod that came out of a Peugeot design contest.

concepts.name: Toyota i-unit
concepts.fact: A one-seat electric pod that sat upright in town and leaned back for speed.

concepts.name: Mazda Nagare
concepts.fact: Started Mazda's 'flow' design theme, with ripples cut into its sides.

concepts.name: Saab Aero-X
concepts.fact: Instead of doors it has a canopy that slides forward over the nose.

concepts.name: Mazda Taiki
concepts.fact: Part of Mazda's Nagare series; its shape was inspired by flowing air.

concepts.name: Toyota FT-HS
concepts.fact: A front-engined hybrid sports concept that was widely read as a hint of a new Supra.

concepts.name: BMW GINA
concepts.fact: Its skin is fabric stretched over a movable metal frame, so the body can change shape.

concepts.name: GT by Citroën
concepts.fact: Created for the Gran Turismo video game, then built for real.

concepts.name: Lamborghini Estoque
concepts.fact: A four-door Lamborghini saloon with a front-mounted V10.

concepts.name: Mazda Furai
concepts.fact: A race-car-based rotary concept that was later destroyed by fire during a Top Gear photo shoot.

concepts.name: Bertone Mantide
concepts.fact: A one-off coupé built on the chassis of a Chevrolet Corvette ZR1.

concepts.name: Bugatti 16C Galibier
concepts.fact: A four-door Bugatti saloon study that was never produced.

concepts.name: Infiniti Essence
concepts.fact: A hybrid grand tourer for Infiniti's 20th anniversary.

concepts.name: Citroën Survolt
concepts.fact: A small electric two-seat sports car study.

concepts.name: Jaguar C-X75
concepts.fact: First shown with micro gas-turbine range extenders. Stunt versions later appeared in the Bond film Spectre.

concepts.name: Peugeot EX1
concepts.fact: An electric speedster that set records for electric cars, including at the Nürburgring.

concepts.name: Renault DeZir
concepts.fact: An electric coupé that launched Renault's new design language under Laurens van den Acker.

concepts.name: Cadillac Ciel
concepts.fact: A four-door convertible with rear-hinged back doors, shown at Pebble Beach.

concepts.name: Mercedes-Benz F125
concepts.fact: A hydrogen fuel-cell saloon study for Mercedes-Benz's 125th anniversary.

concepts.name: Saab PhoeniX
concepts.fact: Saab's last concept car before the company went bankrupt.

concepts.name: Peugeot Onyx
concepts.fact: A hybrid supercar with hand-shaped copper panels and an interior made from felt and pressed newspaper.

concepts.name: Cadillac Elmiraj
concepts.fact: A large two-door coupé shown at Pebble Beach.

concepts.name: Lamborghini Egoista
concepts.fact: A single-seater built for Lamborghini's 50th anniversary, with a cockpit inspired by an attack helicopter.

concepts.name: Nissan IDx
concepts.fact: Its design was worked out together with young, digital-native drivers.

concepts.name: Lamborghini Asterion
concepts.fact: Lamborghini's first plug-in hybrid study, with a V10 and three electric motors.

concepts.name: Bugatti Vision Gran Turismo
concepts.fact: Designed for the Gran Turismo game; its looks previewed the Bugatti Chiron.

concepts.name: Hyundai N 2025 Vision Gran Turismo
concepts.fact: A hydrogen fuel-cell racer designed for the Gran Turismo game.

concepts.name: Mazda RX-Vision
concepts.fact: A front-mid-engined rotary sports car study shown in Tokyo.

concepts.name: Buick Avista
concepts.fact: A twin-turbo V6 coupé shown in Detroit in 2016.

concepts.name: Cadillac Escala
concepts.fact: A long four-door fastback with curved OLED screens inside.

concepts.name: Renault Trezor
concepts.fact: An electric GT whose whole roof and doors open forward in one piece.

concepts.name: Lamborghini Terzo Millennio
concepts.fact: An electric study with MIT where the carbon body itself would store energy.
